note: Every adopted change since the 2006 rule book, in order, with the baseline sections it touches and the sources that establish it. Proposals that failed stay in rules/sources/. Status: adopted, in practice (described as the working rule with no recorded vote), one season (applied once, not a standing rule), or open (the record does not settle it). Paraphrased, name-free. Built and checked by src/rulebook_ledger.py.

changes.change: Each player locks at his own game's kickoff. A lineup not submitted is copied from the previous week, and the owner can still change any player before that player's kickoff. This closes the gap where an owner could watch a Thursday game before deciding whether to submit a lineup at all. Lineups are set on the league website, not by email or phone.
Players tied for a retainment level all take the higher level, so a level can hold more players than its nominal count.

sources.match: Players tied for a retainment level

changes.change: Trading closes at the trade deadline and reopens after the PDL Super Bowl, instead of after the NFL Pro Bowl.

Claims are processed once a week by the league website (Thursday morning). Waiver order is season-long and rolling: a team whose claim succeeds drops to the bottom. After the run, every player not just dropped is a free agent, first come first served, until his game kicks off.

sources.match: Waiver rules on the new MFL site

changes.evidence: MFL's transaction log puts every waiver run on Thursday morning, between about 9 and 10 am Eastern, and the commissioner confirms it. The 2008 board post had said Wednesday 11:30 pm.

changes.change: Yardage scores 1 point per 10 yards once a threshold is reached: 200 yards passing for a QB, 50 yards rushing or receiving otherwise. This replaces the yardage bonuses. TEs unchanged.
changes.evidence: MFL's scoring rules: QB passing changes from 5 points at 200 and 1 per 10 from 250 (2003 to 2009) to 1 per 10 from 200 (2010 to 2017), and WR receiving loses its 100-yard tier. RB rushing is encoded as 5 points for 50 to 59 yards and 1 per 10 from 60, which scores the same as 1 per 10 from 50.

sources.match: 1 point per 10 yards rushing and receiving

changes.change: The trade deadline moves from the end of week 10 to the end of week 12.
Playoff teams no longer receive $25. The champion takes 75% of the pot and the runner-up 25%.
Entry fee $50.
Because of the NFL lockout, retainments were due at least a week after the lockout ended rather than on the usual date.
Retainments are due two weeks before the draft instead of July 4. Draft availability is still due July 4, and the commissioner sets the draft date then.
Ties for a playoff place are broken by: 1. head-to-head result (skipped when three or more teams are tied), 2. points, 3. a coin toss.
Divisions are redrawn from 2015 and every 5 years after: at the draft, each owner draws a division from a hat at the time of his original first-round pick.
changes.evidence: MFL's division alignment, compared by franchise, is the same 2007 to 2014 and changes for 2015.

changes.change: The eight non-playoff teams draft in order of potential points (the season total had each started his optimal lineup every week), lowest first, instead of by record.
A toilet bowl: the eight non-playoff teams play a bracket in the playoff weeks, and the winner's next entry fee is paid by the other owners.
Entry fee $50 plus $5 for the website and $2 for trophy plates, with food collected at the draft.
Entry fee $50 plus $5 website, $2 trophy plates and $4 toward the toilet bowl winner's fee.
Yardage scores from the first yard, with no thresholds: 1 point per 10 yards rushing or receiving, 1 per 20 yards passing.

sources.match: Yardage scores from the first yard

changes.change: Yardage scores in fractions: 0.1 point per yard rushing or receiving, 0.1 per 2 yards passing.
changes.evidence: MFL's scoring rules from 2018: 0.1 per yard rushing and receiving, 0.1 per 2 yards passing, all from zero.

changes.change: Field goals: 0 to 39 yards 3 points, 40 to 49 yards 5, 50 to 59 yards 7, 60 and over 10.
changes.evidence: MFL's scoring rules: field goals 3, 5 and 10 to 2017, then 3, 5, 7 and 10.

changes.change: 0.5 points per reception, for every position. Passed 10 to 6.
changes.evidence: MFL's scoring rules from 2018: receptions at 0.5 for QB, RB, WR and TE.

changes.change: The draft is on the Tuesday after Labor Day, moving earlier only if the NFL starts week 1 before Labor Day.
Two league officers besides the commissioner: one coordinates the draft (availability, date and place), one the summer meeting.
The original divisions are restored at once, ending the 5-yearly redraw.
changes.evidence: MFL's division alignment for 2019 is the 2007 to 2014 alignment again, and stays so through 2026.

changes.change: A league vote reclassified the hybrid QB/TE player from QB to WR.

sources.match: hybrid QB/TE player from QB to WR

changes.change: A COVID contingency plan set refunds and retainment rules for a shortened NFL season, and a reserve list let players out with COVID or opted out sit off the 20-man roster.
Entry fee the usual $50 plus the website fee, rather than waived for COVID.

For the NFL's 18-week season: the regular season runs through week 14, the playoffs in weeks 15 to 17, and the trade deadline and the retainment-value cutoff each move one week later (values through week 17).
changes.evidence: MFL's schedules: 13 regular-season weeks and playoffs in weeks 14 to 16 every season to 2020, then 14 weeks and playoffs in weeks 15 to 17 from 2021. The extra game is a fourth one against the alternating non-conference division: each division now plays every team in both of its non-division pairings, where before it played 3 of the 4 in one of them.

changes.change: Confirmed: the draft is the Tuesday after Labor Day, and retainments are due two weeks before it.

sources.match: The draft stays on the Tuesday after Labor Day

changes.change: The commissioner may override a player's position on the league website when common sense calls for it. Any owner can raise a case.
The toilet bowl winner chooses between the paid entry fee and a bonus pick between the first and second rounds (pick 17). If the pick is taken, the prize money goes to the championship pot.
Entry fee $65. From the pot: $100 to the trophy and website, then the toilet bowl winner's fee if taken, then 75% of the rest to the champion and 25% to the runner-up.
For a tie of three or more teams, the top team is seeded first, then the tiebreak restarts among the rest for the next seed.
The hybrid QB/TE player is listed as a TE for the season. The poll had tied 4 to 4 between that and making him unavailable, and the commissioner settled it.
The $65 entry fee and payout continue.
Entry fee $100.

A player dropped in the waiver run is a free agent, first come first served, straight after it, instead of waiting a week. A player dropped between the run and his kickoff is available at once, not put on waivers.

sources.match: dropped during the Wednesday waiver run
dropped after the waiver run but before kickoff

changes.change: The hybrid QB/TE player is not available to any PDL team for the season.
Entry fee $100, including league fees.
Rule changes are voted in league polls on the website, open for a week.

sources.match: Rule-change voting runs as league polls

changes.change: Each conference plays a 4-team bracket in week 15 (seed 1 against 4, 2 against 3), conference championships in week 16 and the final in week 17.
In practice a two-team tie goes to the head-to-head winner, and a split head-to-head goes to points.
One injured reserve spot during the regular season, for a player with an official NFL designation (IR, IR designated to return, PUP or NFI).
Payout: 67% to the champion, 20% to the runner-up, 6.5% to third and 6.5% to the top regular-season points scorer.
Entry fee stays at $100.
The last-place team organizes the next summer meeting, so the role rotates each year. The 2026 season's last-place team hosts the 2027 meeting.
The league website is the GitHub site, https://mspinola.github.io/pdl/, replacing the old university address.
